We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions to synthesize target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse structure: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide (cinnamamide) attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the fragment: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N is an amide linking to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So overall: a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings: left phenyl with methyl (p-tolyl) attached to sulfonamide N, sulfonyl attached to second phenyl (para-substituted) bearing the cinnamamide side chain.

We need 3 steps retrosynthesis. The hints: step1: amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). Step2: Doebner modification to make α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. Step3: sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus likely forward synthesis: 1) sulfonyl chloride formation from sulfonic acid? But we can start from sulfonyl chloride reacting with amine (the left phenyl amine). So retrosynthesis: disconnect sulfonamide bond -> left aniline (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonic acid attached to second phenyl (which has the cinnamamide). So step3 (retro) is sulfonamide formation: break N-S bond, giving p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid). We'll propose sulfonyl chloride as precursor.

Next, disconnect amide bond: break C-N between carbonyl and aniline (cinnamamide). Retro amide formation: gives carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The aniline is the same as the aniline attached to the sulfonyl? Wait the aniline is part of the cinnamamide side chain: Nc3ccccc3N (that's an aniline with an extra NH? Actually it's an aniline with an amino group at para? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an amino at position 1 and another amino at position? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the nitrogen attached to carbonyl is attached to aromatic carbon (C=O)N-Ph-NH2? The SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N. So it's a phenyl ring with an NH attached to carbonyl (amide) and also an NH2 substituent at the other position (para?). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (anilide) which also has an NH2 group (para). So the amide precursor is the aniline (para-aminophenyl) as nucleophile.

Thus retro step: break amide to give α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (cinnamic acid derivative) attached to phenyl sulfonyl? Wait the α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to the phenyl ring (the second phenyl). Actually the target: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the second phenyl (c2ccc...cc2) has the cinnamamide substituent at para position. So the carboxylic acid precursor would be the same phenyl with α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) attached (i.e., p-(cinnamic acid) phenyl). That can be made via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (p-formyl phenyl) and malonic acid.

Thus retro step2: disconnect the C=C double bond formation: break the double bond to give aromatic aldehyde (p-formyl phenyl) and malonic acid (or its derivative). So we can propose that the phenyl with aldehyde (p-formyl phenyl) is precursor.

Thus overall three steps:

1) Sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride (derived from sulfonic acid of phenyl-sulfonyl). The sulfonyl chloride precursor is the phenyl sulfonyl chloride bearing the cinnamic acid substituent (or after step2). So after step2 we have phenyl-sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl that later will have the cinnamic acid side chain. So we need to have that phenyl-sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) as precursor. That can be obtained from the phenyl sulfonic acid (Ar-SO3H) which can be derived from step2? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is independent of the side chain; we can have the phenyl ring with sulfonyl chloride and also the aldehyde (or after step2). But the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring; the side chain (cinnamic acid) is attached to same phenyl ring at para position. So we need a precursor that is a phenyl ring bearing both a sulfonyl chloride and an aldehyde (or after step2). However step2 will convert aldehyde to α,β-unsaturated acid, not to aldehyde. So the order: first we make the aldehyde (p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride) then Doebner to get α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) attached to phenyl sulfonyl chloride. Then sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine to give final product.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

Target -> disconnect sulfonamide -> gives p-toluidine (C c1ccc(N)cc1) and intermediate A: phenyl sulfonyl chloride with cinnamamide side chain? Wait after sulfonamide formation, the sulfonyl chloride reacts with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide. So intermediate A is the sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl bearing the cinnamamide side chain (i.e., Ar-SO2Cl where Ar = c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2). So A SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2S(=O)(=O)Cl. plus the methyl on left phenyl is separate.

Thus step1 (retro) yields A and p-toluidine.

Step2: disconnect amide: A -> break amide to give B (phenyl with α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). B is phenyl with α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) attached and sulfonyl chloride. So B SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Cl)cc2S(=O)(=O)Cl? Wait the amide carbonyl becomes acid chloride? Actually retro amide formation: we break C-N bond, giving carboxylic acid (or acid derivative) and amine. The forward amide formation uses coupling agent, not acid chloride. So the precursor could be the carboxylic acid (cinnamic acid) attached to phenyl sulfonyl chloride. So B SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2S(=O)(=O)Cl. (carboxylic acid). Then coupling with aniline (c3ccccc3N) gives amide.

Step3: disconnect α,β-unsaturated acid formation: B -> break double bond to give aldehyde (p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride) and malonic acid (or its derivative). So precursor C: c2ccc(C=O)cc2S(=O)(=O)Cl (aryl aldehyde with sulfonyl chloride). And malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH) as separate reagent.

Thus three steps.

Now we need to provide JSON route with type nodes.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We can search for templates matching sulfonamide formation, amide coupling, Doebner modification.

Search for sulfonamide formation: functional_groups_formed = ["sulfonamides"] we already got templates. Choose one with high similarity. Template ID 733 (reaction_id) maybe template_id is the same as reaction_id? The field is reaction_id. We'll assume template_id = reaction_id. Use 733.

For amide coupling: functional_groups_broken = ["amide"] we earlier searched but got many. Need a template that forms amide from acid + amine. Let's search again with functional_groups_formed = ["amide"] maybe.
